In the Fortress repo at /home/user/fortress, every clean build regenerates ~1000 checked-in generated Java sources whose only diff is a header line like: `@version Generated automatically by ASTGen at <date/time>`. I need to know (a) exactly which code produces that timestamp line, and (b) the original rationale for including a timestamp, if any is discoverable, and (c) the cleanest place to patch it out or normalize it. Be very thorough.

Investigate:
1. ASTGen is vendored at ProjectFortress/third_party/astgen/astgen.jar (it's a tool from Rice University's JavaPLT group, related to plt.jar/DrJava). Unzip it into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/bdff267d-67dc-5bb9-b970-8c3dfaa634b6/scratchpad/astgen-jar (use `unzip -o -q`) and check whether it contains .java sources or only .class files. Search for the string "Generated automatically" or "ASTGen at" in whatever it contains (for .class files, use `grep -l` on binary or run `javap -c` / use `strings`). Identify the class and, if source is present, quote the code that formats the date.
2. Also check whether the timestamp text might instead come from Fortress's own build: grep the Fortress tree (ProjectFortress/astgen/, build.xml files, any *.java under ProjectFortress/src that mentions ASTGen) for "Generated automatically" — maybe a Fortress-side template or the .ast file's textual header options contain it. Look at ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast header/options section.
3. Check the OTHER generated-file families for their own timestamp headers: the Rats!-generated parser (search a couple of files under ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser* for "Rats" or timestamp lines; xtc.jar is at third_party/xtc/xtc.jar), and FortressAst.scala / Operators.java (find what generates them — likely code in ProjectFortress/astgen or build.xml tasks) — quote each distinct header format and what writes it.
4. Git archaeology for rationale: `git log --diff-filter=A --oneline -- ProjectFortress/third_party/astgen/astgen.jar` and early commits touching ProjectFortress/astgen/; also `git log -S "Generated automatically" --oneline | tail` to find the first commit introducing files with that header; show its commit message. Any comments near the generation code about versioning/timestamps.
5. Answer: where exactly can we intercept? E.g. if astgen.jar contains sources we could patch and rebuild; or if the date comes through a template/option we can change in Fortress.ast or build.xml; or worst case a post-generation sed step in build.xml (identify exactly which ant target runs astgen — quote it from the relevant build.xml).

Return a structured report: (1) producer of the timestamp for each generated-file family, with file/class names and quoted code where available; (2) any discovered rationale (commit messages, comments, tool docs); (3) recommended patch point(s) ranked, with exact locations. Note: a build/test suite is running in this repo — do NOT run ant, do NOT write anything inside /home/user/fortress; extract jars only into the scratchpad path given above.

Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   Fri Aug 21 15:10:00 2026 +0000

    Fix BCEL mojibake (upstream Apache's own damage) and revive bin/fortress_leaks
    
    Mojibake: 8 vendored org/apache/bcel files carried 23 literal U+FFFD
    replacement characters in comments. Provenance nailed down by comparing
    against Apache's released sources jars from Maven Central: bcel-6.2 AND
    bcel-6.10.0 both contain the identical U+FFFD bytes at the same spots, so
    the corruption happened upstream at Apache (an ISO-8859-1 to UTF-8
    conversion that replaced the non-ASCII bytes instead of transcoding them),
    was never fixed there, and was vendored faithfully by pluckyporcupine's
    graft. Two classes of damage, two fixes:
    
    - 17 section signs in JVMS/vmspec citations (e.g. "JVMS 5.4.3.5",
      "vmspec2 3.3.3") restored to the section sign across StackMap,
      ObjectType, ReturnaddressType, ReferenceType (8), Const,
      InstConstraintVisitor (2), Pass2Verifier. Const.java lines 455-456
      already carried intact section signs, confirming the file's mixed
      encoding history upstream.
    
    - 6 mangled German umlauts sat in two GraphicalVerifier comments
      ("Frames ueberpruefen, die voreingestellte Groesse haben" etc.) —
      JBuilder GUI-designer boilerplate auto-generated in German locale by
      the JustIce verifier author's IDE, describing the plain Swing
      pack()/validate() calls below them (GUI window frames, not JVM stack
      frames). Removed as non-actionable noise, along with the third,
      undamaged German line ("Das Fenster zentrieren"). Comments only;
      zero behavioral change.
